questions.question: What does it mean for $E\subseteq X$ to be disconnected?
options: Open sets $V,W$ covering $E$ with $E\cap V$ and $E\cap W$ disjoint, at least one nonempty
Open sets $V,W$ covering $E$ with $E\cap V$ and $E\cap W$ disjoint and both nonempty
Every point of $E$ is isolated from the rest of $X$ by its own small open ball
Open sets $V,W$ covering $E$ with $E\cap V$ and $E\cap W$ nonempty, possibly overlapping

questions.question: Which of the following subsets of $\mathbb{R}$ is disconnected?
options: Every singleton set
Every interval
The image of a connected set under a continuous function
$\mathbb{Q}$

questions.question: What does the result called continuity preserves connectedness say?
options: If $f$ is continuous and $E$ is connected, then $f(E)$ is connected
If $f$ is continuous and $E$ is disconnected, then $f(E)$ is disconnected
If $f$ is continuous and $f(E)$ is connected, then $E$ is connected
If $E$ is connected, then $f(E)$ is connected for any function $f$

questions.question: In a discrete metric space, what can be said about a set with at least two points?
options: It is always connected
It is connected only if it is an interval
It is disconnected
It has no open subsets

questions.question: Open sets $V,W$ separate a set $E$. What does $E\cap V\cap W=\varnothing$ require?
options: The sets $V$ and $W$ must be equal.
The set $E$ must have no elements.
The sets $V$ and $W$ cannot overlap anywhere.
No point of $E$ belongs to both $V$ and $W$.

questions.question: In $\mathbb{R}$, which set is connected by the interval characterisation?
Which subset of $\mathbb{R}$ is disconnected while its closure is connected?
options: $\mathbb{Z}$
$\mathbb{R}\setminus\{0\}$

questions.question: Which subset of $\mathbb{R}^2$ is connected?
options: $\{(x,0)\colon x\in\mathbb{Q}\}$
$\{(x,y)\colon x\neq y\}$

questions.question: Let $X$ be a space in which open sets are defined. Which condition is the definition of a subset $E\subseteq X$ being connected?
options: $E\neq\varnothing$ and no open sets $V,W$ covering $E$ make $E\cap V$ and $E\cap W$ disjoint and both nonempty.
$E$ has an open cover $\{V,W\}$ for which the pieces $E\cap V$ and $E\cap W$ are disjoint and both nonempty.
$E$ is nonempty and cannot be written as a union of two disjoint nonempty subsets.
$E$ is nonempty and every open cover of $E$ contains a finite subcover of $E$.

questions.question: Under the definitions of this course, how is the empty set $\varnothing\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ classified?
options: It is neither connected nor disconnected.
It is disconnected, since any two disjoint open sets cover it.
It is connected, since it cannot be split into two pieces.
It is both connected and disconnected.

questions.question: Which of the following subsets of $\mathbb{R}$ is disconnected?
Open sets $V,W$ cover $E\subseteq X$ with $E\cap V\cap W=\varnothing$, but $E\cap W=\varnothing$. What can be concluded about $E$?
options: Nothing yet: this cover is not a disconnection, and another open cover might still split $E$.
$E$ is disconnected, because the pieces $E\cap V$ and $E\cap W$ are disjoint.
$E$ is connected, because this cover fails to split it into two nonempty pieces.
$E$ is connected, because $E\subseteq V$ for a single open set $V$.
